headline: Developing a US magnesium plant using proprietary hydrometallurgical IP to target a market that is 100% import-dependent, 90% from China; first production targeted around 2030 with 60%+ of capacity already under supply agreements
reasoning: Latrobe Magnesium has developed a hydrometallurgical process that leaches magnesium from fly ash and ferronickel slag, and is now proposing to build a commercial-scale plant in the United States. The US is currently 100% import dependent on magnesium, with 90% sourced from China, creating significant sovereign supply-chain risk for defence, automotive, and aerospace industries. The company is in advanced negotiations to secure funding and commercial agreements, with a timeline of approximately six months to lock those in and a further year of engineering studies, pointing to first magnesium production around 2030. Latrobe already has 32 ktpa of offtake letters of intent, representing over 60% of the proposed project's capacity. Available US government funding pathways and a binding MOU with SLN for feedstock supply are cited as key de-risking factors.
quote: The US is currently 100% import dependent on its magnesium and 90% of that comes from China. So we're looking at securing funding and locking away some of those commercial agreements that we require in place to get that shored up. So that's, you know, in our estimates, probably going to take around six months. And then when you look then around the types of studies and engineering that we need to do to get this project off the ground, it should take in the order of about a year. So when you put those two things together, we're looking at potentially having first magnesium around 2030 or the start of 2030. In our announcement this morning, we highlighted that we got 32 KTPI of supply, which is over 60% of the projects, which is really pleasing given that we're at this stage of maturity.
